properties.description: As built 2026-09-20. THE PIECES: the prepare pass now answers `{status: needs_llm, prompts, gap: {id, title, why}}`. The prompt is composed by joining the gap's title and description in one statement (detect.rs), and only the joined string came back — so flo2, which wants the CONTEXT folded into a model turn it already pays for rather than a phrased question bought with a second turn, split that string on the literal 'Why it matters:'. That marker is in no schema and rewording the template is legitimate for any release; flo2 declared it as its single breach of the black-box rule and guarded it with a test. The two-phase protocol is UNCHANGED. THE REFUSAL: a replayed gap that is no longer open was already refused with good prose and nothing else, so a consumer could only tell it apart by matching that prose — and flo2 therefore re-ran detect_gaps before EVERY send, a whole graph computation per click, purely to know whether a chip was stale. The refusal now carries `reason: gap_closed` and the id in the error's data. Test: crates/reflow2-mcp/tests/a_composed_prompt_serves_its_pieces.rs (the pieces are the values the prompt was built from, asserted against the composed text; a stale gap refuses with the reason, the id, and the prose intact).
properties.name: The first gap-prompt reply carries the gap's own pieces, and a gap that has closed refuses with a reason a consumer can branch on
